description:
Make the build-policy script fail when a built jit executable links libgit2 or OpenSSL, so the native dependency cannot return through another crate.

## Background

- `scripts/rust-build-budget.sh` runs after compilation in `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` and checks build profiles and dependency features from injectable inputs, each failure mode with a fixture test in `crates/jit/tests/scratch_build/rust_build_budget_checker_tests.rs` that needs no compilation (`scripts/rust-build-budget.sh:12`).
- Nothing checks what the built executables link. Before libgit2's removal, the `jit` binary's dynamic section named `libgit2`, `libssl` and `libcrypto`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The script fails, naming the executable and the library, when a built `jit` or `jit-server` executable declares a dynamic dependency on `libgit2`, `libssl` or `libcrypto`. It fails closed (exit 2) when the tool it reads dynamic sections with is missing on an ELF host.
- [hard] REQ-02: The dynamic-dependency listing is an injectable input, and fixture tests cover a clean listing and each banned library without compiling.
- [hard] REQ-03: The check passes on the current tree.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.
title: Build-policy check rejects native git and OpenSSL linkage
